title: Pane drop edge strips are hit at the origin but drawn at the pane area
body:
`Layout::drop_at` in `panes.rs` tests the pointer cell against edge bands that start at zero: `column < EDGE_BAND`, `column >= body.columns - EDGE_BAND`, `row < EDGE_BAND` and `row >= body.rows - EDGE_BAND`. `draw_drop` draws the four strips as `CellRect { columns: EDGE_BAND, ..body }` and the like, which start at `body.column` and `body.row`. Since the top bar and sidebar landed, `frame::pane_area` returns an area at column 3 or 24 and row 1, and `pointer_cell` hands `drop_at` absolute cells. On a 120-column window with the sidebar open:

| strip | drawn at | hit at |
|---|---|---|
| left | columns 24 to 25 | columns 0 to 1 |
| right | columns 94 to 95 | columns 94 to 119 |
| above | row 1 | row 0 |
| below | one row above the bottom | one row above the bottom |

The zone-to-`Drop` mapping (`None => Swap`, `Some(side) => Split`) is written in both functions, and `body()` returns `self.area` unchanged.

## Proposal

One `edge_strips(area) -> [(Side, CellRect); 4]` built from `area.column` and `area.row`. `drop_at` tests `strip.contains(column, row)` and `draw_drop` draws the same strips. `drop_zones` returns `(Drop, CellRect)` so the mapping is written once. `body()` goes. A test with an area that does not start at the origin pins it.
